items.title: Len Manno Interview, 1959-02-06
items.q: I never worked with them they were in San Antonio when I knew them

ctx.x: well he in other words the drummer should have a sense of phrasing and meter and all of that just like the trumpet player absolutely that's the way I see it so he's playing a sort of our counterpoint in a way huh I mean you might even stretch it and call it that and he'll fill in holes and stuff that's right that's right

I think I think it I think that his rhythm should make musical sense rather than to show what a technician he is where so many of the fellas that today are playing so-called progressive they completely get lost in fact you can sit over there and pat your foot and it might be 15 bars it might be 19 bars and three quarters or it never comes out even all of a sudden he decides to hit a symbol and all the boys come in but you can't you can't pat it out and I think it a drummer above all people should stay and meet…
